chapters.title: Why it really ended (your side of it)
chapters.teaser: Not who was right. What your soul was doing while it fell apart.

chapters.title: Your breakup pattern
chapters.teaser: How you end things, how you grieve, and the habit that slows you down.

chapters.title: Why you keep checking
chapters.teaser: What the pull back toward them is really asking for.

chapters.title: So, will they come back? The honest answer
chapters.teaser: What a chart can and can't tell you, and the question that matters more.

chapters.title: If they ever reach out
chapters.teaser: Three questions to ask before you reply, built for your soul.

chapters.title: What you do now
chapters.teaser: The next small steps that help, whatever they decide.

text.why-it-ended: Sin Metal is the jewel: refined, precise, beautiful under pressure. You have taste and standards, and you notice when something is off by a millimetre. In your last relationship you may have felt quietly disappointed for a long time, holding back criticism and polishing things alone. Or one careless word cut deeper than they ever knew. Jewels are hard, and they still scratch. If the ending involved hurt pride, or a sense that they never really saw your worth, that's the core of it. Look at how much you kept inside just to stay graceful.
text.your-breakup-pattern: You break up beautifully. Sin Metal stays composed, says the right things, looks wonderful the following week. Inside, you replay details: what you wore, what you should have said instead. Your pattern is perfectionism about the ending itself, needing to exit with dignity, needing to understand exactly where it went wrong. You may also judge yourself harshly for choosing them in the first place. Go easier on yourself. Picking someone who turned out to be wrong isn't a flaw in your taste. It's what happens to everyone who has a heart and uses it.
text.the-pull: What pulls you back is often the idea of them. Sin Metal falls for the polished version: who they were at their best, who they could become. You may miss the potential more than the actual person. And if they ended it, the sting of rejection makes your pride want a rematch. Be honest about which one it is. If it's potential, remember that potential isn't a person you can hold. If it's pride, the most elegant answer is a good life that you're genuinely enjoying, for yourself and not for an audience.
text.the-honest-answer: Nobody can read another person's decision from your birth date. That stays theirs. What's yours is your standard. Sin Metal knows its worth but sometimes accepts less to avoid looking difficult. If you're wondering whether they'll come back, ask a different question: would they meet the standard I actually have, the one I never said out loud? If not, the question answers itself. If yes, the next step would be honest communication, including the small hurts you swallowed along the way. A jewel doesn't become less precious by saying that scratched.
text.if-they-reach-out: If they reach out, you'll want to write the perfect reply. Draft it, then delete half. Sin Metal tends to over-polish and under-say. Work out what you actually feel and write that, plainly. If you want to talk, suggest it. If you don't, a gracious short message is entirely you. Watch for one thing: are they apologising for specifics, or just saying they miss you? Specifics matter to you, so let them matter. Don't accept a vague I miss us when what you need is a real conversation about what happened.
text.what-you-do-now: Treat yourself like the jewel you are, but not like a fragile one. Sin Metal restores through beauty and order. Clean your space. Buy the flowers. Wear the thing you've been saving for some imaginary better day. Then do something where you're allowed to be imperfect: a beginner class, a messy art project, karaoke with friends. Spend time with people who make you laugh at yourself. Your sensitivity is a real strength. It just needs a break from scanning for flaws, especially your own, which you find faster than anyone.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your standards aren't too high, Sin. They're just yours.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then why keep them secret for the whole relationship?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Choosing wrong once doesn't mean your taste is broken.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You miss their potential. Potential doesn't text back.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say the small hurts out loud next time.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Best revenge? A great life. Not a perfectly worded reply.

spring.intro: A jewel in spring sits in a garden full of things to admire. Wood ruled your birth season, Sin, and Metal shapes Wood, so you were born with a sharp eye and an appetite for beautiful options. In love you have taste. You knew exactly what you wanted the relationship to look like, and you noticed every way it didn't. After the breakup you may be weighing it like a purchase: was it worth it, did you settle, should you go back to it? That framing will keep you circling. Spring Sin does best when the question shifts from was this good enough to was I myself in it. Shine is easier when you're not polishing for someone else.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're reviewing your ex like a handbag return. Two stars, would not rebuy?

summer.intro: A jewel born in summer knows heat. Fire ruled your season, Sin, and Fire tests Metal, so you grew up under pressure to stay polished while things got hot. You're sensitive, proud and graceful in a crisis, at least in public. In the relationship, criticism probably cut deeper than they realised. You may have absorbed small comments for months. The breakup can feel like a final verdict on your worth, which is why checking is so tempting: you want to know whether they regret it. Summer jewels are formed by heat, not ruined by it. The pressure made you clearer. Their opinion of you was one light source. It was never the whole room.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Their opinion was one lamp, Sin. You still sparkle in every other light.

autumn.intro: Autumn is jewel season, Sin. Metal ruled your birth month and doubled your own element, so your standards, pride and sense of self are strong and well defined. In love that makes you discerning and hard to fool. It also makes you hard to reach. You might have kept part of yourself behind glass the whole relationship, and the other person sensed it. After the breakup the glass case is locked tight. You look perfect. You may be checking their profile while telling everyone you're over it. Strong Sin needs to remember that being admired and being known are different things. The next time someone gets close, let them see a scratch. It's still a jewel.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Over it, you say. While viewing their story at 1:47am. Sure, Sin.

winter.intro: A jewel in winter water glitters under ice. Water ruled your season, Sin, and Metal generates Water, so your sparkle flows out as emotion, insight and very good one-liners. You probably understood the relationship better than you let on, and noticed its cracks early. After the breakup you're likely clear-eyed and still sad, which is a strange pairing. Winter Sin can over-wash a memory: rinsing it until it's flawless, or rinsing it until it's ruined. Neither version is the real one. The pull back usually comes from the flawless version. Write down both, the good and the hard, in plain words. A clean stone is an honest stone, not a perfect one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write the good and the hard side by side. Both were true.

strength.strong: Your jewel is well set, Sin. Plenty of Metal and Earth in your chart give you strong taste, high standards and a clear sense of your own worth. In love that keeps you from settling. In a breakup it can make you severe: every flaw in them catalogued, every mistake of yours locked away. You may be telling yourself you're entirely fine. The blind spot is pride that won't let you be seen missing someone. If you're tempted to reach out, check whether it's love or wanting to win the final scene. You don't need the last word to shine.
strength.weak: With little support for your Day Master, Sin, your shine depends a lot on how others see you. In love you may have polished yourself constantly to stay chosen: right outfit, right reply, right mood. Every criticism landed as a scratch. After the breakup you might be reading their silence as a final grade on you. It isn't. A jewel's worth doesn't drop because one person stopped looking. Spend time with people who admire you without conditions, and practise being seen unpolished. Your value was never theirs to set.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and answers, even in heartbreak. You want a plan for getting over it, maybe even a plan for getting them back. Slow down. Not everything grows on schedule, and some things need to just sit for a while. Ask for help instead of turning healing into a project. For balance, let a little Metal in: declutter, finish old things, clear out the drafts folder. A clean edge helps Wood stop reaching for what's already gone.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means fresh starts feel heavy. After a breakup you might stay in the same place, emotionally and literally, for longer than you'd like. That isn't weakness. It just means new growth needs a nudge. Small steps work best: a new route to work, one new class, one new person a week. Get outside in the mornings and keep something green near you. You don't need a whole new life. You need one new branch, and then another.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes you feel everything at full volume. A breakup can feel like an emergency, with urges to text, post, or fix it all tonight. Your passion is real, but heat isn't a strategy. Before any big move, sleep on it. Cool down with water: swimming, long showers, quiet evenings at home. Talk to your calmest friend before your most exciting one. Let the fire warm you instead of burning through your peace.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means joy and visibility don't come easily, and after a breakup you might go dim for a while, hiding from people and from fun. Turn the lights back on gently. Sunshine, music, dancing in the kitchen, one social plan a week even when you'd rather stay in. Letting people see you is the medicine here. Warmth doesn't only live in romance. It's in friends, in laughter, in simply being out in the world.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you hold on: to routines, to memories, to the hope that things will settle back into their old place. Stability is your gift, but in heartbreak it can turn into staying stuck. Shake the ground a little. Move the furniture, take a short trip, try something unplanned. Let some Wood energy in, growth and new beginnings. You can keep what was good and still leave room for something new to grow.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means life can feel unsteady, and a breakup can knock away what little ground you had. You might feel scattered, unsure where to put your feet. Build structure gently: regular meals, a steady bedtime, one place at home that's only yours. Cook something. Walk somewhere. Lean on the people who are reliable. Stability first, big decisions later. You need solid ground under you before deciding anything about the past.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal makes you sharp and decisive, sometimes too quickly. You may have cut the relationship off cleanly and then refused to look at what you feel. Or you judge yourself harshly for every mistake you made in it. Soften the edges. Let Water in: rest, tears, music, journaling. Feeling the grief isn't the same as reopening the door. You can keep your boundaries firm and still let your heart thaw.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard, so after a breakup you might keep the door half open, answer every message, or stay friends when it hurts. Practise clean edges. Mute without guilt. Box up their things. Say no without explaining. White and silver, tidy spaces and finished tasks all help your chart. A boundary isn't cold. It's how you protect the part of you that's still healing.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means you think and feel deeply, maybe endlessly. After a breakup you might drift through memories, analyse every detail, and lose sleep to what-ifs. Your intuition is a gift, but it needs riverbanks. Add some Earth: routines, cooking, walks, people who ground you. Give overthinking a time limit. Feel it fully, then get up and do one ordinary thing.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means rest and reflection get skipped. You may rush past the breakup, staying busy so you never have to sit with it. That works until suddenly it doesn't. Build in quiet on purpose: slow mornings, water by your bed, a few lines in a journal at night, a bath instead of another plan. Let yourself feel without fixing. Intuition grows when you give it some silence.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: So much Wood. You've drafted three versions of 'hey, random but' already.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy wants a goal. Give it your own plans, not their inbox.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: every feeling is a five-alarm emergency. It's a breakup, not an inferno.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is beautiful. Let it cool before you hit send on anything.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth. You'd still be in that relationship purely out of habit.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Just make sure you're loyal to yourself too.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. You cut them off cleanly, then reread everything at midnight.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Being firm protected you. Being gentle with yourself will heal you.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've cried to three songs and written a novel in your notes app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Feeling deeply is a gift. Just come up for air sometimes.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make moving on feel stuck. Small new routines count as growth.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: You haven't changed anything since the breakup, including your lock screen. Start there.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make joy feel far away. Borrow some from a loud friend.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: You stopped having fun when they left. Fun was never theirs to take.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth can make everything feel unsteady. Simple routines will hold you.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no anchor. You re-decide whether to text them every hour.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal makes boundaries tricky. You're allowed to say no to your own phone.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means you'll answer at 2am. Put the phone in another room.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make grief hide. It's okay to let it surface slowly.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: You said you're fine twelve times today. Water would like a word.

gap-wood.title: The jewel who noticed everything
gap-wood.text: You put care into every message and got 'ok 👍' back. You rewrote your texts to get the tone right, you planned the dinner, you chose the gift with real thought, and they took it all as normal, because to a Gap Wood effort is just what decent people do. They didn't praise it. You noticed every time. Then you said something precise about their shirt, or the way they talked over the waiter, and they heard judgement where you meant care. In public they could be blunt in ways that made you want to sink into the floor. In private you held the hurt politely, sharpened it a little, and let it out in small, exact cuts. What aches is feeling unseen by someone you admired. They were upright and honest, and you wanted that honesty to include 'you look beautiful' once in a while. You still miss their steadiness, the way they never played games. Next time, say needs plainly, without polish. 'I'd love it if you noticed when I try.' Rough-edged sentences are allowed. They're often the ones that land.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, you deserved specific praise. Asking for it plainly isn't needy.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, 'ok thumbs up' to a carefully written text is a crime in some countries.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Different currencies, real love. The exchange rate was the problem.

eul-wood.title: Pruned by the scissors
eul-wood.text: You loved a beautiful plant and couldn't stop trimming it. Your Eul Wood ex was warm, adaptable, easy to love, and you saw everything they could be with just a few adjustments. A better job. A smarter coat. A friend who wasn't quite worth their time. You offered your notes with care and good taste. They heard 'you're not enough', and adapted, and their adapting made you respect them a little less, which you'd never admit. Then both of you went quiet in that polished way: careful texts, read receipts, the long wait to see who'd be vulnerable first. Neither of you was. Your sting is pride. You were trying to help, and it still came out as hurt. Their softness is what you miss. They made you feel less sharp, less alone with your standards. Try a week of saying only appreciation to the people close to you. No improvements. Just what's already good. If it feels unbearable, that's useful information about what you carried into that relationship.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, your eye for detail is a gift. Not every detail needs a note.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, you're not a bonsai. Stop letting people shape you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Someone has to say 'I miss you' first. Usually it's the brave one.

byeong-fire.title: Sunlight on a jewel
byeong-fire.text: You were the jewel and they were the sunlight, and for a while you felt seen in a way you rarely are. A Heavenly Combination, everyone could tell. Your Byeong Fire ex was warm, generous, proud of you in public. But they were also loud where you're quiet, careless where you're careful. They forgot the detail you'd mentioned twice. They made a joke at the wrong moment. You rewrote your messages until they were perfect; they replied in four seconds with three emojis and didn't seem to notice the work. When you felt overlooked, you pulled back or got precise and cool, and they felt your standards as a test they kept failing. The love was real and you still felt unappreciated in the small moments, which happen to be your favourite moments. Their warmth is the hook. Nobody made you feel so golden. Say what matters before it becomes a grudge. 'It meant a lot when you remembered.' 'I was hurt you forgot.' Plain, early, kind. Jewels don't have to hide their scratches.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, you deserved to have the effort noticed. Ask for it out loud.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, three emojis in reply to a perfect paragraph. Think about that.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Heavenly Combination. Still needs small, daily care.

jeong-fire.title: A flame near silver
jeong-fire.text: You loved a flame that wanted to be very, very close, and closeness that intense made you want to step back and fix your hair. Your Jeong Fire ex loved with full attention: long messages, deep feelings, a need for reassurance you found hard to give on demand. You value poise. When you made a precise comment, a small observation about their tone or a choice, they took it deeply to heart, and you didn't realise how hard it landed. Both of you crafted messages, reread them, overanalysed the reply, and both of you retreated when it stung. The tension sat between you like a held breath. Being called cold when you were actually overwhelmed is the part that stings. Their devotion is what pulls you. Nobody else has wanted you that wholeheartedly. Tell people what overwhelm feels like for you, before it happens. 'When I go quiet, I'm processing, not leaving.' It turns your silence from a mystery into a message, and gives warmer people something to hold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, you weren't cold. You were overwhelmed. Say that next time.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Jeong, rereading their text nine times doesn't decode it. Asking does.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A silly selfie can melt a week of tension. Try it.

mu-earth.title: The mountain guarding the gem
mu-earth.text: You were the gem and they were the mountain, and you felt safe in a way you rarely do. Your Mu Earth ex was steady and protective and refreshingly unbothered by drama. But they were also not a detail person. You rewrote your messages until each word was right; they replied in six words. You hinted for weeks that something mattered, a date, a gesture, a way you liked to be treated, and they didn't catch it, and then you were hurt and they were baffled. You found yourself critiquing their simplicity, and you could see it landing, quietly. Feeling unappreciated by someone who absolutely did appreciate you, just not in words, is a strange ache. The safety is what you miss. With them, your sensitivity never needed defending. Say what matters directly, instead of hinting. 'Our anniversary matters to me, can we plan something?' Mountains respond beautifully to clear instructions. And remember that a short reply from a steady person often carries more than a long one from anyone else.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, their short reply still meant 'I'm here.' Mountains are like that.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, 'nice' is not a compliment. Be specific or be silent.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Steady love for a precious thing. It was real.

gi-earth.title: The jeweller's workbench
gi-earth.text: You loved someone almost as careful as you, and it turned out two careful people can be exhausting together. Your Gi Earth ex worried; you critiqued. You'd make one precise comment, about a plan, a word, the way they folded the towels, and they'd worry about it for days, quietly. You found them fussy, anxious. They found you cold, demanding. Neither of you says hard things directly, so the tension lived inside polite sentences and long pauses. Texts took ten minutes to write and ten to decode. You thought you were helping, and they felt judged, and that gap is what aches. Their attention is what you miss. They noticed your effort, appreciated your standards, took care of you in practical ways that made your life smoother. Let one imperfect thing stand this week without comment. Notice the urge to fix it, and let it go. Your precision is a gift, but at home the kindest thing is sometimes to put the tools down.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: A three-line text took ten minutes. On both ends. Exhausting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, not every detail needs your note. Some need your hug.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Send the silly one. Nobody ever broke up over a dumb meme.

gyeong-metal.title: Steel and silver
gyeong-metal.text: You're the silver and they were the steel. Same metal, very different finish. Your Gyeong Metal ex said what they thought, bluntly, without decoration. To you, that felt crude, sometimes even careless. They scratched your polish without noticing, a comment at dinner, a joke in front of your friends, and you responded with a sharp, quiet line that they very much noticed. Your precision felt like nitpicking to them. Their directness felt like disrespect to you. Both of you are proud, and neither of you went first with sorry. Being loved roughly by someone who honestly didn't know they were being rough is a particular kind of tiring. Their certainty is what you miss. You liked how sure they were, how they never played games. Say it plainly. They missed subtext, and so do many people. 'That comment embarrassed me.' No layers, no wit. It feels exposed. It also gets heard, which is the whole point. Your elegance survives a plain sentence. It might even shine more.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, they missed your subtext. Every single time. Stop sending it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, soften the delivery. Keep the honesty.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Same metal. Different polish. Equal pride.

sin-metal.title: Two jewels in one box
sin-metal.text: Two Sin Metals in one box: dazzling, delicate, and very easily scratched. You understood each other's standards and taste without a word. Your texts were witty, precise, loaded with subtext, and you both reread before sending. But both of you are sensitive to criticism, and both of you are naturally critical. Small comments became wounds. Both of you wanted to be appreciated, and both of you waited for the other to go first. Pride made reconciliation slow; a cold war could last a week over a single remark about someone's shoes. Comparison crept in too. Who was more admired, more successful, more put together at the party. You were so alike that every flaw you saw in them felt like a mirror, which made it hard to be generous. The recognition is what pulls you. Nobody else ever understood your standards without explanation. Go first with appreciation. Specific, generous, unprompted. And send something dumb now and then, a blurry photo, a terrible pun. Perfection is lonely in pairs.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You understood each other's standards. That's rare and lovely.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: A cold war over shoes. Two jewels. Very on brand.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Go first with appreciation. It costs nothing and softens a lot.

im-water.title: A jewel washed in the river
im-water.text: Clarity, sparkle, freedom. Your Im Water ex washed over you like a river over a jewel, and you shone. They were clever, free-spirited, and genuinely fun to talk to. But their unpredictability unsettled you. You like things polished and planned; they showed up late, underdressed for the dinner you'd booked weeks ago, cheerful and unbothered. You noticed. You commented. They found your critiques annoying; you found their carelessness hurtful. When they drifted for a few days, you felt neglected and filled the silence with theories, each one more elaborate than the last. You felt like the only one who cared about the details, and details are how you love. That's why it cut. The freedom is what you miss. With them, you loosened up, left the house without checking the mirror twice, and liked yourself more. Separate the person from the plan. Someone being late isn't someone not caring. And don't read too much into gaps in texting. Their silence was usually about them, not you. Your sparkle doesn't need anyone's punctuality to exist.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, late and underdressed to the dinner they booked weeks ago? Wow.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, their silence was rarely about you. Breathe.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Notice the effort. It's free and it matters enormously.

gye-water.title: Silver in the rain
gye-water.text: Silver in the rain: delicate, intuitive, quietly beautiful. That was you and your Gye Water ex. The trouble was that hurt sent you both inward. You'd make one small precise comment; they'd go quiet; you'd read the quiet as coldness and withdraw too; and then you were both sitting in separate rooms of silence, each waiting for the other to knock. Neither of you likes direct conflict, so small hurts piled up. Their moods confused you; your critiques stung them. Texts were thoughtful and sometimes delayed, and both of you overthought every delay. There was so much tenderness, and so little of it said out loud. What pulls you back is how deep it went. They understood your sensitivity without needing it explained, and you never had to apologise for feeling things at full volume. Agree with yourself that a late reply is just a late reply. And say the warm thing first, before the precise thing. 'I love this, one small thought.' Gentleness first, notes second. It's the same honesty, wearing softer gloves.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, 'that hurt' said gently beats a week of quiet.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, your 'small comment' wasn't small to them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A late reply is just a late reply. Repeat it.
